Package org.dellroad.muxable.simple

Class SimpleMuxableChannel

java.lang.Object
org.dellroad.stuff.net.SelectorSupport
org.dellroad.muxable.simple.SimpleMuxableChannel
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, AutoCloseable, Channel, MuxableChannel<Pipe.SourceChannel,Pipe.SinkChannel>
public class SimpleMuxableChannel extends SelectorSupport implements MuxableChannel<Pipe.SourceChannel,Pipe.SinkChannel>
An implementation of the MuxableChannel interface that multiplexes nested channels over a single underlying ByteChannel (or ReadableByteChannel, WritableByteChannel pair) using a simple framing protocol.

The nested channel data and NestedChannelRequests share the same underlying "real" channel, so any one left unread for too long can block all the others. This implementation only guarantees that "senseless" deadlock won't happen (see MuxableChannel).

Protocol Description

After the initial connection, each side transmits a protocol cookie followed by its current protocol version. Once so established, the protocol simply consists of frames being sent back and forth. A frame consists of a channel ID, an optional flags byte, a payload length, and finally the payload content. The channel ID and length values are encoded via LongEncoder.

The channel ID is negated by the sender for channels created by the receiver; this way, the receiver can differentiate a local channel ID (negative) from a remote channel ID (positive). Reception of a frame with a channel ID of zero means to immediately close the entire parent connection.

Each side keeps track of which channel ID's have been allocated (by either side). Reception of a remote channel ID that is equal to the next available remote channel ID means the remote side is requesting to open a new nested channel; the subsequent payload becomes the data associated with the request, and a flag byte is sent after the channel ID specifying the Directions for the new nested channel.

Reception of zero length payload implies closing the associated nested channel (however, this does not apply to the initial frame that opens a new channel, so it's possible to request opening a new channel with zero bytes of request data). Closing a nested channel always means closing both directions.

Note that it's possible for one side to receive data on a nested channel that it has already closed, because that data may have been sent prior to the remote side receiving the local side's close notification. Such data is discarded.

Java NIO

This is a Java NIO based implementation. The underlying channel(s) must be SelectableChannels, and the nested channels returned by this class will use the SelectorProvider given to the constructor (by default, the one associated with the input channel).

Because an internal service thread is created, instances must be explicitly start()'d before use and stop()'d when no longer needed. When this instance is stop()'d, the underlying channel(s) are closed.

Invoking close() on this instance has the same effect as invoking stop().

Instances are thread safe.

  • Method Details

    • newNestedChannelRequest

      public SimpleNestedChannelRequest newNestedChannelRequest(ByteBuffer requestData, Directions directions) throws IOException
      Description copied from interface: MuxableChannel
      Create a new nested channel, or pair of nested channels, scoped to this instance.

      The remote side will be notified by the appearance of a corresponding NestedChannelRequest in the queue returned by MuxableChannel.getNestedChannelRequests() (with the input and output channels reversed, of course). The delivery of requests on the remote side is guaranteed to preserve order (but only to the extent order is well-defined on the sending side, i.e., there is a "happens before" relationship).

      Specified by:
      newNestedChannelRequest in interface MuxableChannel<Pipe.SourceChannel,Pipe.SinkChannel>
      Parameters:
      requestData - data to supply to the remote side (via NestedChannelRequest.getRequestData())
      directions - which of input and/or output to create
      Returns:
      the newly created nested channel(s)
      Throws:
      IOException - if an I/O error occurs

    • getNestedChannelRequests

      public BlockingQueue<SimpleNestedChannelRequest> getNestedChannelRequests()
      Description copied from interface: MuxableChannel
      Access the queue of incoming NestedChannelRequests initiated from the remote side.

      Each NestedChannelRequest corresponds to a remote invocation of newNestedChannelRequest(). Moreover, the order of requests is preserved.

      Because the remote side can close a nested channel at any time, it is possible that the new channel associated with an incoming NestedChannelRequest has already been closed in a subsequent message from the remote peer by the time the original NestedChannelRequest is pulled from this queue. In such a case, the nested channel's input and output streams will throw IOException on first access.

      Note: no special change happens to the returned BlockingQueue once this instance is closed; instead, new requests simply stop appearing. Therefore, after closing this instance, any thread(s) that are blocked polling for new data may need to be woken up via Thread.interrupt().

      Specified by:
      getNestedChannelRequests in interface MuxableChannel<Pipe.SourceChannel,Pipe.SinkChannel>
      Returns:
      queue of NestedChannelRequest initiated from the remote side
